scenes.narration: Sixty-one. That's the number Israel's next leader needs, and polls suggest nobody has it.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real close-up of a hand dropping a paper ballot into a ballot box, shallow depth of field, warm light, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: Israel votes today for all 120 seats in its parliament, the Knesset, its first election since the October 7, 2023 attacks.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real exterior of the Knesset parliament building in Jerusalem, daytime, wide establishing shot, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: It's widely seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu. Both camps are defined as pro- or anti-Netanyahu.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real view of a text card on a deep navy background reading first election since Oct 7, 2023, clean typography, no conflict imagery, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: Polls average former army chief Gadi Eisenkot's party, Yashar, narrowly ahead of Likud, by about two seats.
scenes.on_screen_text: Yashar ahead of Likud by ~2 seats
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real two-bar poll graphic on a navy background with text only, no faces, labels Yashar and Likud, bars nearly equal, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: But seats are counted in blocs. Per the Jerusalem Post average, the opposition bloc leads by about 4.5 seats, yet neither bloc reaches 61. Netanyahu's bloc polls 48 to 51.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real graphic of a horizontal line marked 61 with two bars falling short, navy and amber, credit text Source: Jerusalem Post poll average (25 Oct), 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: The swing factor? Arab parties, polling about 14 seats, up from 10 now. Some partners in Eisenkot's bloc are wary of working with them.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real two-bar graphic on navy showing 10 seats now versus about 14 polled, clean text only, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: No party has ever won a majority alone. The president picks whoever is likeliest to form a government, not automatically the biggest party.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real interior of a parliament debating chamber with rows of seats, a 61/120 counter overlay, soft light, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: They get 28 days, extendable by 14. If that fails, others can try. If all fail, Israel votes again.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real four-step graphic on navy: President consults, 28 days (+14), Others try, New election, arrows between steps, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: Coalition or another election: which comes first?
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real Meera speaking to camera at dusk, raised eyebrow, questioning expression, city skyline softly blurred behind, 9:16 vertical
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: Exit polls tonight. Final results take days. Follow for the result explained.

scenes.speaker: Arjun
